title: Exponent compatibility before the site-unit map
statement: Fix a finite purity datum P, a separated finite-type P.field.k-scheme T, annihilating exponents r+1 and r′+1, a bounded-below pro-etale complex K and a constructible finite-Tor ordinary representative Ke with comparison isomorphism eK. The canonical coefficient transition through the specified inverse-limit Tate line, tensored with p*K, intertwines sourceComparison(r′).inv followed by comparison of sourceCoordinates(r′).hom and the ordinary conjugate at r′ with the corresponding composite at r. These are the maps before boundedSiteRho and the representative target map. All maps are those of [def-pur-coordinate-line-adjunction-maps] and [def-pur-affine-line-purity-source].

source.place: First two sentences and final comparison paragraph, expanded coordinate-line calculation

proof.text: For r<=r′ the normalized root transition preserves both projective decomposition components. Cancel the inverse decomposition and project to its second component to identify the normalized projective traces. Naturality of the open counit gives the same equation for restricted affine traces.

source.place: Ordinary affine-line composite adjunction and its final site-comparison paragraph

proof.text: Use projection naturality and the actual inverse-projection counit formula. Invert the projection square and apply the affine trace equation. This gives compatibility of the actual ordinary coefficient counits. Transpose under the fixed Brown adjunction; naturality of its Hom bijection identifies the ordinary conjugates.

source.place: Ordinary affine-line composite adjunction and its final site-comparison paragraph

proof.text: Exact site comparison carries this equation to the two sites. The source tensor/pullback comparisons are natural in the coefficient, and the root-normalized Tate site comparisons identify their transition with coefficientTwistIso(r) followed by its inverse at r′. Conjugate by sourceComparison. For unordered exponents pass through max r r′ and cancel the common isomorphism. Equal exponents, empty schemes and zero coefficients obey the same identities.

theorem coordinate_line_conjugate_exponents
    (P : WeilConjectures.PurityFiniteSetting.{u}) (T : Scheme.{u})
    (aT : T ⟶ Spec (.of P.field.k))
    [LocallyOfFiniteType aT] [QuasiCompact aT] [IsSeparated aT] [IsNoetherian T]
    (r r' : ℕ)
    (hA : ((P.coefficients.l ^ (r + 1) : ℕ) : Ring P) = 0)
    (hA' : ((P.coefficients.l ^ (r' + 1) : ℕ) : Ring P) = 0)
    (hP : IsUnit (P.coefficients.l : Γ(ProjectiveLine T, ⊤)))
    (hX : IsUnit (P.coefficients.l : Γ(AffineSpace PUnit.{u + 1} T, ⊤)))
    (K : DerivedCategory.Plus
      (Sheaf (Scheme.ProEt.topology T) (ModuleCat.{u + 1} (Ring P))))
    (Ke : Etale.DerivedCategoryModule (Ring P) T)
    (hKe : Etale.DerivedCategory.constructibleFiniteTor
      (ModuleCat.{u + 1} (Ring P)) T Ke)
    (eK : (VectorIntegrationSite.comparison (Ring P) T).obj Ke ≅ K.obj) :
    (tensorCoefficientIso (Ring P) T _ _
      (coefficientTwistIso P.coefficients.l P.extension (P.level - 1) T r hA hP hX ≪≫
        (coefficientTwistIso P.coefficients.l P.extension (P.level - 1) T r' hA' hP hX).symm)
      K.obj).hom ≫
    (sourceComparison P.coefficients.l P.extension (P.level - 1) T r' hA' K.obj Ke eK).inv ≫
    (VectorIntegrationSite.comparison (Ring P) (AffineSpace PUnit.{u + 1} T)).map
      ((sourceCoordinates P T r' hA' Ke).hom ≫
        (comparison (Ring P) (P.coefficients.l ^ (r' + 1)) hA' T
          (pow_pos (Fact.out : P.coefficients.l.Prime).pos _)
          (by simpa only [Nat.cast_pow] using (primeUnit P T aT).pow (r' + 1))).hom.app Ke) =
    (sourceComparison P.coefficients.l P.extension (P.level - 1) T r hA K.obj Ke eK).inv ≫
    (VectorIntegrationSite.comparison (Ring P) (AffineSpace PUnit.{u + 1} T)).map
      ((sourceCoordinates P T r hA Ke).hom ≫
        (comparison (Ring P) (P.coefficients.l ^ (r + 1)) hA T
          (pow_pos (Fact.out : P.coefficients.l.Prime).pos _)
          (by simpa only [Nat.cast_pow] using (primeUnit P T aT).pow (r + 1))).hom.app Ke)
